description: Single-source builtin TYPING as data: name x operand type patterns -> result type + coercions, consumed by both Compiler.builtin/4 and ElixirMode.builtin/4, which keep only emission. Decisions (grilling 2026-10-12, recorded as ADR-0008): builtins only, constructs stay code; row vocabulary capped at the regular majority (type variables, type classes, result = constant or operand reference, coercion spec), irregular builtins keep bespoke clauses but get a typing: :bespoke row so the table stays total; enforcement by table-generated agreement kernels (one tiny kernel per concrete type combination, both modes, assert_agrees) - a missing clause, wrong coercion and semantic drift all fail the same test. SEMANTICS stay written twice on purpose (Elixir mode is the oracle) - see ADR-0008 before deduplicating further. CONTEXT.md 'Builtin' added.

comments.text: Re-check before starting (flagged in the 2026-10-12 review wrap-up): the '~80% of builtins fit the capped row vocabulary' estimate came from one ~70-line excerpt of each emitter, not a census. Step one: census every Compiler.builtin/4 and ElixirMode.builtin/4 clause and count what actually fits. Known blind spot to close: typing: :bespoke rows carry no operand-type patterns, so the Q25 enforcement (table-generated agreement kernels) cannot generate kernels for them - yet bespoke rows are exactly where typing drift survives. Likely fix: bespoke rows carry concrete example signatures (not patterns) to generate agreement kernels from; decide with the census in hand. If the bespoke fraction is high, revisit the vocabulary cap itself.

Census done (step one): all 25 clause pairs of Compiler.builtin/4 x ElixirMode.builtin/4 fit the capped vocabulary - bespoke fraction is ZERO, not ~20%. Needed vocabulary, confirmed exhaustive: concrete types (i64/u64/f64/bitstring/arr(u8)), classes :int (i64|u64) and :number (int|f64), a same-scalar type var (min/max [t,t] -> t), a same-element array var (copy/copy_back arr(e)...arr(e) -> arr(e)), results as a constant or an operand reference (rotl -> type of x; trunc of an int -> its own type), ordered rows per name (div [i64,i64]->i64 before [int,int]->u64), and a per-operand coercion map (-> i64 or -> f64). The typing: :bespoke escape hatch stays in the schema for the future but no current row uses it, so the generated-kernel blind spot flagged earlier is moot. One generation caveat found: u64 is not a kernel parameter type, so :int-class instantiations at u64 need an in-kernel idiom (i64_to_u64 or masked arithmetic) or stay covered by the existing suite - decided during implementation.

title: Grow Defk.Builtins into the builtin signature table (ADR-0008)
